attention_tiled — LLMCORE attend op

• Data kinds: tokens × tokens × tokens → tokens

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.attention_tiled(query, key, value, tile: 'int' = 64, mask=None, window=None, scale=None) -> 'np.ndarray' (to call the implementation directly, import llmcore; llmcore.attention_tiled(query, key, value, tile: 'int' = 64, mask=None, window=None, scale=None) -> 'np.ndarray'; from the registry, opsllmcore.get("attention_tiled"))

Usage

Attention with tiles + online softmax (the core of FlashAttention) → tokens. Not an approximation.

Dao et al. 2022. Reads key/value tile rows at a time and adds them up while correcting the running maximum and denominator on the spot. The only intermediate matrix it builds is (T, tile); (T, T) is never built — the speed comes not from approximation but from where things are kept. The relative difference from attention_softmax is 1.2e-15 even with 128 tiles (8.2e-16 with 1 tile, so 128 times as many tiles gives only 1.5 times the difference).

Args:

query: (T, d) float.

key: (S, d) float.

value: (S, dv) float.

tile: number of key/value rows read at once. Smaller means a smaller intermediate matrix and more tiles.

mask: None / "causal" / "window" / (T, S) bool array.

window: window width when mask="window".

scale: score multiplier. None means 1/√d.

Returns:

tokens (T, dv) float: matches attention_softmax to machine precision.
